title: My week at the animal shelter

task.situation: Last week you spent five days of work experience at an animal shelter. Now you want to write about the week on your personal blog.
task.instruction: Write a blog post. In your blog post you should:
points: outline what you did during the week
describe one animal that you will never forget
explain what you have learnt from the experience

words.short: Give your blog post a title. Write around 200 words.
words.long: Give your blog post a title. Write around 250 words.

task.de: Blogbeitrag über eine Schnupperwoche im Tierheim (Titel, Username, Datum, persönlicher und lockerer Ton, Kurzformen erlaubt, Leser:innen ansprechen, zum Kommentieren einladen). Drei Inhaltspunkte: Aufgaben beschreiben, ein besonderes Tier, was ich gelernt habe. Den Titel wählen wir ganz zum Schluss.

focus.label: present perfect
focus.note: Marked: verbs in the present perfect (have / has + past participle), used for experiences, results that matter now and periods up to now. Past simple verbs with finished times (last week, on Wednesday) are not marked.

gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Namen für das Tier. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: Introduction: how do we open our blog post?
steps.de: Der erste Absatz eröffnet den Blogbeitrag. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words: say where the blogger spent the week.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben, wo die Person, die den Blog schreibt, die Woche verbracht hat.

options.label: Greet the readers
options.text: {{Hi everyone! [[I’ve just finished]]}} a week of work experience, and guess where I spent it? At an animal shelter! {{It was tiring and messy,}} but it was also one of the best weeks ever.
options.why: A greeting and a question speak to readers like friends. ‘I’ve just finished’ shows that the week has only just ended.

options.label: Start with a question
options.text: {{What really happens}} behind the doors of an animal shelter? {{Last week I found out.}} I spent five days of work experience there, and I already miss the animals.
options.why: A question makes readers curious, and ‘Last week I found out’ answers it in a short, punchy sentence.

options.label: Introduce the week
options.text: This blog post is a report on the work-experience placement which was completed at an animal shelter from Monday to Friday. The tasks that were carried out and the knowledge that was gained are described below.
options.reject: Far too formal for a blog post: no ‘I’, mostly passive verbs (‘which was completed’, ‘were carried out’) and stiff phrases such as ‘the knowledge that was gained’. A blog post sounds personal and talks to its readers.
options.rejectDe: Viel zu förmlich für einen Blog: kein „I“, fast nur Passiv und steife Wendungen. Ein Blog klingt persönlich und spricht die Leser:innen an.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: what did we do during the week?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: unsere Aufgaben im Tierheim. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe the tasks in your own words. Use the past simple for finished times.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Aufgaben mit eigenen Worten beschreiben. Für abgeschlossene Zeitpunkte das Past simple verwenden.

options.label: Day by day
options.text: {{So what did I do all week? On my first morning,}} the staff showed me around and gave me rubber boots. {{From then on,}} I cleaned kennels, filled water bowls and walked the dogs. {{By Friday,}} I knew the names of all twenty-three dogs!
options.why: A question picks up the introduction, then time phrases lead readers through the week. Finished times go with the past simple.

options.label: From Monday on
options.text: On Monday I have cleaned all the kennels, and the chef of the shelter showed me how to prepare the food. I never saw so many dogs in my whole life! In the afternoons I took them for walks and brushed the cats.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘On Monday I have cleaned’ (→ On Monday I cleaned), ‘the chef’ (→ the manager) and ‘I never saw … in my whole life’ (→ I’ve never seen … in my whole life).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: On Monday + Present perfect → On Monday I cleaned, chef (= Koch, Köchin) → manager, I never saw … in my whole life → I’ve never seen … (Erfahrung bis jetzt).

options.label: Hard work
options.text: {{Shelter work is no holiday: [[I’ve never worked]] so hard in my life!}} {{Every morning I}} cleaned cages, washed food bowls and carried heavy bags of dog food. {{In the afternoons, I}} walked the dogs and brushed the cats, the best part of the day.
options.why: A strong personal statement leads from the introduction into the week, then details in the past simple.

steps.q: Who or what else impressed us during the week?
steps.de: Der Absatz geht weiter: Menschen im Tierheim oder ein besonderer Tag. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own details about the people at the shelter or the special day.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Details zu den Menschen im Tierheim oder zum besonderen Tag ergänzen.

options.label: The volunteers
options.text: {{The shelter could not work without its people.}} {{Most of them are volunteers}} who come after work or at weekends, whatever the weather. {{One woman [[has helped]] there for}} more than twenty years, and the dogs run to the fence when she arrives.
options.why: Turns from the animals to the people who look after them. ‘Has helped … for more than twenty years’ is still true today.

options.label: A happy day
options.text: {{The happiest moment of the week came on Thursday.}} A family took home a young dog after three visits, as the staff want to be sure that every animal finds the right home. {{Since that day, the family [[has sent]]}} the shelter two photos of a very happy dog.
options.why: Adds one special moment to our week. Past simple for Thursday, present perfect with ‘since that day’ up to now.

steps.q: Which animal will we never forget?
steps.de: Wählt das Tier, über das wir im nächsten Absatz schreiben.

options.label: An old dog
options.teaser: A twelve-year-old dog that most visitors walk straight past.

options.label: A shy cat
options.teaser: A black cat that hides from everybody.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: which animal will we never forget?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: das Tier, das uns in dieser Woche besonders berührt hat. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe the animal and one moment with it in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann das Tier und einen Moment mit ihm mit eigenen Worten beschreiben.

options.label: Tell the story

map.old: My favourite was {ANIMAL}, an old dog that most visitors walk straight past. Finally, on my very first morning, I said hello through the fence. After that, we went for a slow walk together every afternoon. At first, on my last day, I almost cried when I said goodbye.
map.shy: My favourite was {ANIMAL}, a shy black cat that hid from everybody. Finally, on my very first morning, I said hello through the cage door. After that, I sat next to the cage with a book every afternoon. At first, on my last day, I almost cried when I said goodbye.

options.reject: The time words are mixed up: ‘Finally’ introduces the first morning, and ‘At first’ introduces the last day. Readers can’t follow the order of events.
options.rejectDe: Die Reihenfolge-Wörter sind vertauscht: Finally steht beim ersten Morgen, At first beim letzten Tag. So versteht man die Reihenfolge nicht.

options.label: Describe the animal

map.old: {{Of all the animals, the one I’ll never forget is}} {ANIMAL}, a twelve-year-old dog with a grey nose and kind brown eyes. {{Sadly, this dog [[has lived]] at the shelter for}} more than a year because most visitors want puppies. Every afternoon we walked slowly around the block.
map.shy: {{Of all the animals, the one I’ll never forget is}} {ANIMAL}, a black cat that hid under a blanket all day. {{Sadly, this cat [[has lived]] at the shelter for}} almost a year because shy cats are rarely adopted. Every day I sat by the blanket and talked softly.

options.why: ‘Of all the animals’ leads from the whole week to one animal. ‘Has lived … for more than a year’ is still true today.

options.label: One special moment

map.old: {{One animal, though, stole my heart:}} {ANIMAL}, an old dog that most visitors walk straight past. On Wednesday, I sat down in the kennel with a book, and after a while a grey head landed on my knee. {{Nobody [[has ever trusted]] me like that.}}
map.shy: {{One animal, though, stole my heart:}} {ANIMAL}, a shy black cat that hid from everybody. On Wednesday, I sat quietly next to the cage with a book, and after an hour a little black paw touched my hand. {{Nobody [[has ever trusted]] me like that.}}

options.why: ‘One animal, though’ turns from all the work to one animal and zooms in on one moment. The last sentence sums up a life experience.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: what have we learnt?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: was wir aus der Woche mitnehmen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain in your own words what the blogger has learnt.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten erklären, was die Person, die den Blog schreibt, gelernt hat.

options.label: Lessons about animals
options.text: {{Animals such as {ANIMAL} [[have taught]] me a lot.}} They need fixed routines and people who stay calm, even on busy days. {{[[I’ve also realised]] that}} a pet is a promise for ten or fifteen years, not a quick birthday present.
options.why: The first sentence links the animal of the last paragraph to the lessons. The present perfect shows that they still matter now.

options.label: Lessons about myself
options.text: {{Looking back, [[I’ve learnt]] a lot about myself.}} I used to think I was too impatient for quiet work. {{Now I know that}} I can stay calm when a frightened animal needs time, and [[I’ve started]] to think about a job with animals.
options.why: ‘Looking back’ turns to the whole week. Compares the past (‘I used to think’) with now: very personal, which suits a blog.

options.label: What I learnt
options.text: I learnt a lot at the shelter. I learnt that animals need fixed routines. I learnt that a pet is a promise for many years. I learnt that I can be patient. I learnt that I want a job with animals.
options.reject: The ideas are good, but every sentence starts with ‘I learnt’. Vary your sentences: Now I know that …, I’ve also realised that …, The week has taught me …
options.rejectDe: Gute Ideen, aber jeder Satz beginnt mit „I learnt“. Abwechslungsreiche Satzanfänge verwenden.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end our blog post?
steps.de: Der letzte Absatz greift die ganze Woche kurz auf und lädt zum Kommentieren ein. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then sum up the blogger’s week in one sentence and finish with your own question or invitation to the readers.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Woche der Person, die den Blog schreibt, in einem Satz zusammenfassen und mit einer eigenen Frage oder Einladung an die Leser:innen enden.

options.label: Sum up, then ask the readers
options.text: {{All in all, the week [[has given]] me dirty boots, lots of new ideas and}} a friend called {ANIMAL}. {{So, what about you? [[Have you ever adopted]]}} a pet from a shelter? Let me know in the comments below!
options.why: Sums up the week in one sentence, then a question with ‘Have you ever …?’ invites comments.

options.label: Recommend the experience
options.text: {{My tip: if you’re still looking for work experience,}} try an animal shelter. You’ll get dirty, but you’ll learn a lot and maybe find a friend like {ANIMAL}. {{[[Have you ever done]] work experience}} somewhere unusual? Tell me in the comments!
options.why: Turns the whole week into a tip for readers and ends with a question they can answer in the comments.

steps.q: Now that the blog post is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Der Titel kommt zuletzt und soll neugierig machen und zum Inhalt passen.
steps.own: Short and catchy: make readers curious about our week.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und treffend: Der Titel soll neugierig auf unsere Woche machen.

options.label: A playful title
options.why: Short and playful. It shows the hard work and the happy animals.

options.label: A personal title

map.old: What an old dog taught me
map.shy: What a shy cat taught me

options.why: Personal and curious: readers want to know what we learnt.

options.label: A title with a picture
options.text: Five days of paws, fur and mud
options.why: Readers can see and almost smell the week at the shelter.

checks.en: A title that makes readers curious, with user name and date under it
Each content point has its own body paragraph, in the order of the task
All three content points: our tasks, one special animal, what we have learnt
Every body paragraph starts with a sentence that links back to the paragraph before
Past simple with finished times (last week, on Wednesday)
Present perfect for experiences and results that matter now
Informal, personal register: contractions are fine, mistakes are not
The conclusion looks back at the week and invites readers to comment

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Blogbeitrag (A2+/B1) über eine Schnupperwoche im Tierheim und übt dabei den Unterschied zwischen Past simple (abgeschlossene Zeitpunkte) und Present perfect (Erfahrungen, Ergebnisse, Zeiträume bis jetzt) sowie Blog-Konventionen.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (eine Garnitur pro Person), Hefte bereitlegen. Beamer im Vollbild. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Absatz, bei Bedarf +1. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum rechts oben, darunter „Blog post“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Dann 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt), darunter Username und Datum in einer Zeile (wie am Beamer). Fünf Absätze, jeder nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion. In der langen Fassung geht Body 1 ohne neue Zeile weiter. Present-perfect-Formen grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Kopf, 7 Entscheidungen (inklusive Wahl des Tiers) à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 20 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (ca. 60 min): wie kurz, dazu eine Fortsetzung von Body 1 (Freiwillige oder ein besonderer Tag); das sind eine Entscheidung und rund 45 Wörter Abschreiben mehr. In einer Doppelstunde die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen nutzen und die Hausübung zu zweit beginnen. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Kopf; pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 5 min Checkliste. In einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss noch abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben lassen; Schluss fertigschreiben und eigenen Titel finden als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (ca. 70 min): gleicher Rhythmus wie kurz, dazu die Fortsetzung von Body 1 mit ca. 5 min Schreiben. In einer Doppelstunde danach eine Vergleichsrunde zu zweit.
teacher.traps: Intro C (LSR): viel zu förmlich für einen Blog (kein „I“, fast nur Passiv, steife Wendungen). Body 1 B (LSA): On Monday I have cleaned, chef statt manager, I never saw … in my whole life statt I’ve never seen. Body 2 A (CC): Finally und At first vertauscht, Reihenfolge unklar. Body 3 C (LSR): jeder Satz beginnt mit „I learnt“. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Aufbau: Jeder Text hat fünf Absätze (Einleitung, drei Hauptabsätze, Schluss); die lange Fassung macht Body 1 länger, sie fügt keinen Absatz hinzu. Fokus: markiert sind nur Present-perfect-Formen; nach Body 1 lohnt eine Minute an der Tafel: Signalwörter für das Past simple (on Monday, last week, every afternoon) und für das Present perfect (ever, never, just, since, for … bis jetzt). Kohäsion: Die Klasse achtet darauf, wie jeder Hauptabsatz an den vorigen anschließt (So what did I do …?, One animal, though, …, Animals such as …) und wie der Schluss die ganze Woche aufgreift. Das Tierheim und alle Personen sind erfunden; Schnuppertage im Tierheim sind je nach Einrichtung und Alter unterschiedlich geregelt. Für die Namenslücke einen erfundenen Tiernamen verwenden, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus einen Satz mit „Have you ever …?“ an die Leser:innen. Hausübung: Blog-Kommentar (ca. 80 Wörter) als Antwort auf den Beitrag, mit einer Frage an die Person, die den Blog schreibt, und einem eigenen Tipp für eine Schnupperwoche.
